keyPhrases.text: treats the play as though it were carved entirely in air
risks turning 'Death of a Salesman' into a funhouse
only the great De Shields is able to stylishly pull off

reasoning: Review is predominantly critical of the production's approach, describing it as insubstantial ('carved entirely in air'), minimal ('barest minimum'), and inappropriate ('funhouse'). Only praise is for one performer (De Shields). The criticism outweighs the single positive element.
